caption: "interest rates today" — 100,000+ searches in 24 hours. Swipe for 10 things most people don't know about today's Fed decision.

Why: on September 16 the Federal Reserve raised its benchmark rate a quarter point to 3.75% to 4%, its first increase since 2023. The vote was 12 to 0. The reason fit in three words: inflation remains elevated.

What most people don't know: nine months ago the Fed was cutting, three meetings in a row at the end of 2025. Now 16 of 18 officials expect another hike this year, and the 30-year mortgage is already at 7.19%.
Very simply put: the cheap-money reversal took nine months, and the Fed says it is not finished.
